injuryReports.name: Jayden Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a knee injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Chiefs on Nov. 22. Josh Fryar will likely start at left tackle in Williams' absence.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Roy Lopez
injuryReports.returnComment: Lopez injured his toe in Week 9 against the Seahawks, and he was also working through an ankle issue during Week 10 prep. The sixth-year pro went through pregame warmups, and medical staff gave Lopez the green light to play in Sunday's NFC West showdown. Lopez has accumulated 24 tackles (10 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Lopez (toe/ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Andrew Wingard
injuryReports.returnComment: Wingard's practice reps during Week 10 prep were limited by a groin issue, but the veteran safety was cleared to play in Sunday's NFC West tilt. He's logged 42 tackles (20 solo), one interception and one forced fumble through six regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Wingard (groin) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Hunter Long
injuryReports.returnComment: Long was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the sixth-year pro has been cleared to return from a five-game absence due to a knee injury. He will operate in a rotational role at tight end behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins.
injuryReports.injury: Long (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Joey Aguilar
injuryReports.returnComment: With Jacoby Brissett being traded to Baltimore on Nov. 6 and Gardner Minshew (elbow, IR) out for the rest of the season, the Cardinals overhauled their QB room by signing both Josh Johnson and Aguilar earlier this week, with Carson Beck now serving as the starter. As the emergency third quarterback, Aguilar is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Beck and Johnson leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Starling Thomas V
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Eku Leota
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Hjalte Froholdt
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Jon Gaines II
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Gardner Minshew II
injuryReports.returnComment: Minshew incredibly played through the injury in Week 9, logging all 53 offensive snaps and completing 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in his first start replacing the since-departed Jacoby Brissett. Schefter added that Minshew still is determining the timing of the procedure, but he plans on having it. With Minshew out for the rest of the campaign, rookie third-round pick Carson Beck is taking over under center for the Cardinals.
injuryReports.injury: Elbow

injuryReports.name: Zay Jones
injuryReports.returnComment: Jones signed with the Cardinals' practice squad Oct. 28, and this is his first elevation since joining the organization. The veteran wideout could immediately slide into a major role in Arizona's passing game among a depleted wideout corps that has lost Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) for the season. Jones spent the past two campaigns with the Cardinals, and he caught 12 passes (on 18 targets) for 182 yards over eight games last year.
injuryReports.injury: Jones was elevated from Arizona's practice squad to the active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Zachary Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter will remain on IR for Week 10 and will not suit up for Sunday's divisional contest against the Rams. The defensive tackle logged three consecutive limited practices after being designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Simi Fehoko
injuryReports.returnComment: Fehoko is a 2021 fifth-round pick who turned 29 earlier this month and has been targeted on just two of 37 routes for the Cardinals this year. He mostly seems to have stuck around the league because his size is useful for special teams and blocking, but Fehoko now has a chance to get more snaps on offense, if only because Arizona's WR depth chart has been decimated. He has a chance to start this Sunday against the Rams in QB Carson Beck's first career start.
injuryReports.injury: Fehoko will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Reggie Virgil
injuryReports.returnComment: A 2026 fifth-round pick, Virgil started his career buried on the depth chart before moving up due to injuries and trades. It's not quite the same as earning a starting job, but he should see routes and targets all the same in the coming weeks. Virgil has been targeted on 11 of 56 routes (19.6 percent) and caught just three passes for 54 yards in five appearances. He should get plenty of playing time this Sunday against the Rams in what will be the first career start for rookie QB Carson Beck.
injuryReports.injury: Virgil will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Bam Knight
injuryReports.returnComment: Knight figures to split backfield work with Tyler Allgeier, who played 96 percent of snaps last week when Knight was inactive for a 17-3 loss at Seattle. Knight suffered the concussion in Week 8, shortly after Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle -- an issue that sent the rookie to injured reserve not long after. Love is out for at least three more games, leaving Allgeier and Knight to split backfield work again.
injuryReports.injury: Knight (concussion) is cleared to play Sunday against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Elijah Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: Higgins was scheduled for free agency after this season, and he's taken on a larger role as the year has progressed, helping the Cardinals get by with limited talent at wide receiver. Higgins has 18 catches for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets, serving as a complementary receiving option alongside Trey McBride when the Cardinals use multi-TE formations. Higgins figures to stick in that role long-term and won't be of much fantasy interest unless McBride misses time.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins is signing a contract extension with the Cardinals through 2029, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Budda Baker
injuryReports.returnComment: The star safety has now logged three 11-tackle games this season, and Baker remains one of the bright spots for a Cardinals team that doesn't have many in 2026. The 10th-year pro was mentioned in trade rumors prior to Tuesday's deadline, but he'll finish out the campaign in Arizona. He's up to 62 tackles (29 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. Baker appears headed for an eighth straight Pro Bowl selection.
injuryReports.injury: Baker recorded 11 tackles (three solo) in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Carson Beck
injuryReports.returnComment: Arizona first dealt Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore last Friday, and then Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL in his right elbow during this past Sunday's game at Seattle and will undergo season-ending surgery. That series of events precedes Beck taking over as the Cards' No. 1 signal-caller, and with eight other skill-position players on reserve lists at the moment, the top talents available to the offense will be TE Trey McBride and RB Tyler Allgeier.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Beck will start Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Evan Hull
injuryReports.returnComment: Ten of Hull's 12 snaps came on special teams, and he wasn't bale to connect with Gardner Minshew on the latter's pass attempt early in the third quarter. Hull has yet to log a carry through three regular-season appearances with the Cardinals. However, he could operate as the team's RB2 behind Tyler Allgeier for Week 10 against the Rams if Bam Knight doesn't clear the league's concussion protocol for that contest.
injuryReports.injury: Hull failed to haul in his lone target during the Cardinals' 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Devin Duvernay
injuryReports.returnComment: A two-time Pro Bowl return man, Duvernay played exclusively on special teams over the Cardinals' first seven games of the season, but he's seen his role on offense expand out of necessity following the trade of Marvin Harrison to the Texans along with the season-ending injuries to Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist). For the second straight week, Duvernay logged just under half of the offensive snaps, with his 45 percent share placing him behind only Michael Wilson (83 percent) and Simi Fehoko (49 percent) among the team's wideouts. Head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that Wilson was diagnosed with a neck fracture that will bring an end to his season, so Duvernay could be in line for an even more pronounced role heading into next Sunday's game against the Rams. However, with starting quarterback Gardner Minshew (elbow) also sustaining a likely season-ending injury in the loss to the Seahawks, Duvernay will be on the receiving end of passes from rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will make his NFL debut in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Duvernay registered two catches for eight yards on two targets, returned three kickoffs for 64 yards and brought back two punts for 21 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks.

injuryReports.name: Michael Wilson
injuryReports.returnComment: Wilson's move to IR was merely a formality, after head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that the wideout would be sidelined for the rest of the season after sustaining a fractured vertebra in his neck during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks. Per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Wilson is expected to be in a neck brace for the next six weeks to two months, but the Cardinals don't view the injury as a long-term or career-threatening concern. The 26-year-old receiver will finish the 2026 campaign with 51 receptions for 546 yards and two touchdowns on 88 targets to go with 28 rushing yards on three carries across his nine appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Chad Ryland
injuryReports.returnComment: Ryland played just three snaps during the loss, though he managed to convert his only kick, which came from 28 yards and also served as the team's only points in the game. He now has converted 20 of his 22 field-goal attempts and 16 of his 17 extra-point tries across nine games this season.
injuryReports.injury: Ryland made his lone field-goal attempt during Arizona's loss versus the Seahawks on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Adam Randall
injuryReports.returnComment: Randall has been on injured reserve all season while recovering from a neck injury. He was designated to return Oct. 28 but wasn't activated for Week 8 or Week 9. Randall was a fifth-round selection in April's NFL Draft, so if he's activated and gets into Monday's Week 10 matchup, it will be his NFL regular-season debut.
injuryReports.injury: Neck

injuryReports.name: Jaylinn Hawkins
injuryReports.returnComment: Head coach Jesse Minter ruled out the veteran safety for Monday Night Football following Saturday's practice. It will be the fourth consecutive absence for Hawkins, who is recovering from a knee injury, and that means K'Von Wallace will continue to see more snaps in the secondary. Hawkins' next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Panthers on Sunday, Nov. 22.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Rashod Bateman
injuryReports.returnComment: After being limited at practice Thursday, the starting wideout is in line to face the Chargers on Monday night after being deemed 'FP' on Friday. While Bateman has turned in two consecutive one-catch efforts, there's a chance that working with the team's new QB Jacoby Brissett could spark some added production for the 2021 first-rounder while working alongside top WR Zay Flowers.
injuryReports.injury: Bateman (calf) was listed as a full participant on Friday's practice estimation.

injuryReports.name: Lamar Jackson
injuryReports.returnComment: Minter's statement confirmed previous reports that Jackson is both recovering from a "broken and dislocated thumb" and also that he is facing a recovery timeline of at least six weeks. It did not confirm that Jackson underwent surgery, but per Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com a procedure has been performed, and Jackson is not due back before Week 16. Jackson informed teammates earlier this month that he plans to return this season, but that will hinge on how his recovery progresses and presumably whether or not the Ravens are in playoff contention late in the campaign. Jacoby Brissett, who was recently acquired from the Cardinals, figures to hold down the starting quarterback spot in Jackson's absence.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Kyle Hamilton
injuryReports.returnComment: Hamilton suffered a hip injury during the Week 9 loss to Jacksonville and didn't finish the contest. Now, after logging a full practice Thursday, he is good to go for Monday's game against the Chargers, assuming he doesn't suffer a setback along the way. Hamilton has appeared in all nine games for Baltimore during the 2026 campaign, accumulating 60 total tackles (43 solo), one interception and four additional passes defended.
injuryReports.injury: Hamilton (hip) practiced in full Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Nate Wiggins
injuryReports.returnComment: Wiggins was inactive for the Week 9 meeting with the Jaguars. However, after logging a full practice session Thursday, it appears he is good to go for Week 10 against the Chargers. The 23-year-old has appeared in eight games this season, garnering 24 total tackles (17 solo) and four passes defensed.
injuryReports.injury: Wiggins (illness) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Riley Patterson
injuryReports.returnComment: The Ravens signed Harrison Mevis to their practice squad in addition to signing Patterson to the 53-man roster, but the team intends to utilize Patterson as the kicker for Monday's game. Patterson went 7-for-9 on field-goal attempts in five appearances with the Dolphins this season, with a long of just 41 yards. His career-long made field goal of 54 yards came with Miami last season.
injuryReports.injury: Patterson will be the Ravens' kicker for Monday night's game against the Chargers, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Ryan Neuzil
injuryReports.returnComment: Neuzil had started at center in each of the Falcons' first nine games of the season, but he's expected to fill a more versatile backup role in Baltimore, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. In addition to center, Neuzil is capable of playing both guard spots, so he'll likely be the top candidate to start if Cam Jurgens, John Simpson or Vega Ioane misses time at any point.
injuryReports.injury: The Ravens acquired Neuzil from the Falcons on Tuesday in exchange for guard Andrew Vorhees and a conditional 2028 sixth-round pick, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Jacoby Brissett
injuryReports.returnComment: Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal-caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who currently is on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season. However, he's out for at least three more games, and 4-5 Baltimore's record as the season progresses figures to factor into Jackson's approach to a potential return to action.
injuryReports.injury: Ahead of Week 10, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter noted "I expect (Brissett) to be our starter" next Monday against the Chargers, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Malaki Starks
injuryReports.returnComment: Starks tied for third on his team in tackles during a rather uninspiring performance on both offense and defense by the Ravens. He did make a big play when he forced a fumble that was recovered by Baltimore in the third quarter, but the Ravens turned the ball over on downs on four plays on their ensuing possession. Starks logged 84 tackles over 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, and he's well on his way to surpassing that mark with 55 stops (including 1.0 sacks) through nine contests in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: Starks finished Baltimore's Week 9 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday with four tackles (three solo) and a forced fumble.

injuryReports.name: Roquan Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Smith led his team in tackles on a night when Baltimore had a hard time slowing down the Jaguars' offense. Though he's been bothered by knee and foot issues in recent weeks, the veteran linebacker logged a 95 percent defensive snap share Thursday. Smith is well on his way to another triple-digit tackle campaign with 74 stops, including 2.0 sacks, along with an interception and two forced fumbles through nine contests.
injuryReports.injury: Smith finished with eight tackles (two solo) in Thursday's Week 9 loss to Jacksonville.

injuryReports.name: Derrick Henry
injuryReports.returnComment: With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.
injuryReports.injury: The Ravens aren't expected to deal Henry before Tuesday's trade deadline, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Matt Hibner
injuryReports.returnComment: Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.
injuryReports.injury: Hibner logged one reception for five yards on two targets in Thursday's loss to Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Kobi Lane
injuryReports.returnComment: Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.
injuryReports.injury: Lane did not draw a target Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville.

injuryReports.name: Josh Cuevas
injuryReports.returnComment: Cuevas split time with nine snaps on both offense and special teams. This game marked the fourth time this season that the rookie had zero targets. Prior to Thursday night, the 23-year-old saw multiple targets in four straight games. He will likely have a similar role as the season continues.
injuryReports.injury: Cuevas didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Devontez Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: Walker made little impact in Thursday night's loss, playing 15 offensive snaps behind Ja'Kobi Lane (32), Rashod Bateman (35) and Zay Flowers (37). Walker will likely see a similar role as the season progresses.
injuryReports.injury: Walker didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.

injuryReports.name: Justice Hill
injuryReports.returnComment: Hill provided the sole offensive highlight of the night for the moribund, Joe Fagnano-led offense, making one cut after getting the handoff from the rookie quarterback halfway through the fourth quarter and bursting through the defense up the right side of the field for a 65-yard touchdown run. Hill's yardage total was both a team- and season-high figure for the veteran change-of-pace back, who should benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals whenever the veteran signal-caller is able to take the reins of the offense.
injuryReports.injury: Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Mark Andrews
injuryReports.returnComment: The veteran tight end actually led the Ravens in receiving yards with his modest total, as fill-in signal-caller Joe Fagnano averaged just 3.3 yards per attempt and totaled 60 passing yards overall. Andrews opened the season with back-to-back 49-yard tallies on 10 total catches, but he's been stuck at 28 receiving yards or fewer in his seven subsequent games. Andrews will hope to benefit from the pending trade acquisition of Jacoby Brissett, who should bring some stability and productivity to Baltimore's currently embattled quarterback situation.
injuryReports.injury: Andrews secured both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Joe Fagnano
injuryReports.returnComment: Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve, and the undrafted rookie signal-caller unsurprisingly had a difficult night after also struggling in emergency duty against the Bills just four days earlier. Fagnano had been dealing with an ankle injury stemming from his aforementioned NFL debut and had little practice time on a short week, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle kept the game plan simple and focused on the short areas of the field, resulting in Fagnano averaging just 3.3 yards per attempt. Both of Fagnano's second-half picks also led to Jacksonville field goals, making it a forgettable night overall. With the Ravens reportedly putting the finishing touches on a trade with the Cardinals for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, Fagnano is likely to move into a reserve role as soon as a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.
injuryReports.injury: Fagnano completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while adding three rushes for 13 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Zay Flowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Joe Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (IR, thumb) and Tyler Huntley (IR, toe) out of action, and the rookie undrafted signal-caller averaged a microscopic 3.3 yards per attempt and threw two interceptions. Therefore, Flowers once again put forth a forgettable receiving line, although he at least got on the board with a trio of catches after being blanked on five targets in the Week 8 loss to the Bills. The Ravens tried to boost Flowers' touches with his trio of rush attempts, and he was reasonably effective with those. While fantasy managers have gotten next to nothing from the talented receiver over the last two games, Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore is finalizing a trade for with the Cardinals, could be ready to suit up as soon as a Week 10 home matchup with the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.
injuryReports.injury: Flowers brought in three of six targets for six yards and rushed three times for 17 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night.

injuryReports.name: Dalton Risner
injuryReports.returnComment: Risner and Myles Hinton (illness) are both late additions to Cincinnati's injury report. Jacob Bayer would likely slot in at right guard if Risner cannot play.
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Myles Hinton
injuryReports.returnComment: Hinton appears to have developed an illness over the weekend, and he's now in danger of missing Sunday's AFC North tilt. His absence would result in the Bengals having less depth on the offensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Illness

injuryReports.name: Andrei Iosivas
injuryReports.returnComment: Iosivas was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Steelers despite logging full practices Thursday and Friday. He'll remain on IR for at least one more game, and his next chance to play is Week 11 against the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23.
injuryReports.injury: Thumb

injuryReports.name: Kyle Dugger
injuryReports.returnComment: Dugger has not been cleared to return to practice since suffering a quadriceps injury in Week 7. The reserve strong safety will miss a third consecutive game due to the injury, leaving Russ Yeast and PJ Jules to back up starter Jordan Battle.
injuryReports.injury: Quadriceps

injuryReports.name: DJ Turner II
injuryReports.returnComment: Turner was able to play through his ankle injury in Week 9 against the Falcons, and it now looks like it's behind him entirely. He projects to start at cornerback against a pass-heavy Steelers offense Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Turner (ankle) was a full participant at practice Thursday.

injuryReports.name: Brian Parker II
injuryReports.returnComment: Parker was placed on injured reserve on cutdown day with a designation to return. It appears the 22-year-old has progressed through his undisclosed injury and could be a candidate to return soon. Should he suit up this season, the sixth-round rookie will likely serve in a depth role on the offensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Jalen Davis
injuryReports.returnComment: Davis was placed on injured reserve in late September after suffering a hamstring injury in Week 3 against the Steelers. The Bengals now have 21 days to officially activate the 30-year-old for him to remain eligible to play this season.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Bryan Cook
injuryReports.returnComment: Cook had his most productive outing of the campaign, logging a season-high 10 tackles. The 2022 second-round pick will look to build on this performance and keep producing during the team's Week 10 matchup versus the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Cook registered 10 tackles (five solo) during the Bengals' win over the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Barrett Carter
injuryReports.returnComment: Carter had one of his most productive outings of the season during the victory, as he matched Bryan Cook for the most tackles on the team in addition to recording his first interception of the campaign. The 2025 fourth-round pick has racked up 68 tackles (28 solo), including 1.5 sacks, an interception and two forced fumbles across eight games this season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Carter compiled 10 tackles (two solo), an interception and a pass deflection during Cincinnati's win over the Falcons on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Dohnte Meyers
injuryReports.returnComment: With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve, Meyers has settled in as the Bengals' third receiver behind target hogs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Meyers would need an injury to one of those two to become relevant again in fantasy.
injuryReports.injury: Meyers caught two passes for 47 yards on three targets in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Samaje Perine
injuryReports.returnComment: Perine logged two more carries than Chase Brown in the game, but Brown out-produced him with 57 rushing yards. Perine has continued to operate in a modest role as the Bengals' No. 2 option in the backfield, and he would stand to be a valuable fantasy asset in the case that Brown is forced to miss any action down the road this season.
injuryReports.injury: Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Evan McPherson
injuryReports.returnComment: McPherson was able to convert multiple field-goal tries in a game for the first time since Week 3, nailing a 57-yarder in the final moments of the first half before later adding a 43-yard make in the fourth quarter. The kicker had gone back-to-back games without a field-goal attempt, but he has now gone a perfect 12-for-12 on field-goal tries, including 6-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests this season.
injuryReports.injury: McPherson went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts while making all four of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Mike Gesicki
injuryReports.returnComment: Gesicki entered Week 9 having scored a touchdown in five straight games, and he saw his streak come to an end Sunday. The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week and fifth time this season, but his 11 receiving yards left much to be desired. Gesicki has now reeled in 19 of 26 targets for 252 yards and six touchdowns over eight regular-season games so far this year.
injuryReports.injury: Gesicki caught both of his targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 34-17 win versus Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Chase Brown
injuryReports.returnComment: Samaje Perine actually saw more volume on the ground with 11 carries for 43 yards, but most of his workload came in the fourth quarter as the Bengals were grinding down the clock. Brown has yet to top 80 rushing yards in a game this season and he hasn't gotten into the end zone since Week 1, a disappointing first half of the year for a running back who amassed at least 1,300 scrimmage yards with double-digit scores each of the prior two campaigns. Brown will look for an opportunity to break out in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Brown carried the ball nine times for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Tee Higgins
injuryReports.returnComment: While he didn't see big volume, Higgins made his opportunities count, connecting with Joe Burrow on a four-yard TD in the second quarter and an eight-yard score in the third. Higgins has hit paydirt five times in the last three games, and on the season he's produced a 48-758-6 line on 67 targets through eight contests. He'll look to extend his scoring streak in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North clash with the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Higgins caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over Atlanta.

injuryReports.name: Ja'Marr Chase
injuryReports.returnComment: The superstar wideout hit the ground running in Madrid, capping Cincinnati's first drive with a 47-yard touchdown catch from Joe Burrow. It was Chase's fourth straight game getting into the end zone, a stretch in which he's delivered a stellar 32-435-4 line on 45 targets, and Sunday's 155 receiving yards were a season high. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.
injuryReports.injury: Chase caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons.

injuryReports.name: Joe Burrow
injuryReports.returnComment: It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries.

injuryReports.name: Cedric Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: Johnson suffered an ankle injury last Sunday versus the Titans, and he subsequently followed a DNP/LP/FP practice regimen during Week 9 prep before getting a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's international matchup. Now that he's confirmed to be active, he should be good for his normal 20-30 percent weekly defensive snap share.
injuryReports.injury: Johnson (ankle) is listed as active Sunday against the Falcons in Madrid.

injuryReports.name: Cashius Howell
injuryReports.returnComment: Howell suffered a right wrist injury during Sunday's overtime win against the Titans, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests as a result. The defensive lineman has already undergone surgery, per Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com, and in Howell's absence, Shemar Stewart will stand to see an increase in workload at defensive end.
injuryReports.injury: Wrist

injuryReports.name: Colbie Young
injuryReports.returnComment: Though quarterback Joe Burrow set season highs in passing yards (462) and passing touchdowns (five), Young didn't see any involvement while the targets were highly concentrated among Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown. The fourth-round pick out of Georgia has held a bit role so far during his rookie season, recording two catches for nine yards on two targets through five appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Young went without a target while playing 19 of the Bengals' 74 snaps on offense in Sunday's 43-36 overtime win over the Titans.

injuryReports.name: Joey Porter Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Porter upgraded to limited participation in Friday's practice after missing the first two Week 10 prep sessions and the Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Colts. The cornerback is all set to return to the field alongside DaRon Bland to anchor the Cowboys' secondary for a big matchup with one of the NFC's top contenders.
injuryReports.injury: Porter (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Juanyeh Thomas
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Ribs

injuryReports.name: Jonathan Mingo
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Derion Kendrick
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: P.J. Locke
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Concussion

injuryReports.name: Ajani Cornelius
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Donovan Ezeiruaku
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Jake Ferguson
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: DaRon Bland
injuryReports.returnComment: Bland was added to the Cowboys' injury report Friday after the ankle issue limited his participation in the team's final practice of Week 10, but the injury doesn't look as though it will prevent him from suiting up Sunday. Additionally, Joey Porter (ankle) is listed as questionable but trending toward playing after a one-game absence, so Dallas looks as though it will have both of its top two cornerbacks available versus San Francisco.
injuryReports.injury: Bland (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.

injuryReports.name: James Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: The Cowboys technically still have one elevation to use on Mitchell this season, but they instead will opt to sign him to the active roster for Week 10. His signing gives the Cowboys extra depth at tight end, as the team will be without Jake Ferguson (knee) for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
injuryReports.injury: The Cowboys signed Mitchell from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Israel Abanikanda
injuryReports.returnComment: With Tyler Goodson (knee) on injured reserve and Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the rest of the year, Abanikanda is expected to operate as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for the foreseeable future, starting with Sunday's game against the 49ers. Abanikanda last saw regular-season action in 2023, when he logged 22 carries for 70 yards (3.2 YPC) and added seven catches on 11 targets for 43 yards across six regular-season games with the Jets.
injuryReports.injury: The Cowboys elevated Abanikanda from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Goodson
injuryReports.returnComment: The move comes as no surprise, seeing as Goodson is expected to miss multiple games due to ACL and MCL sprains in his knee that he suffered during the Cowboys' Week 9 victory over the Colts. With Malik Davis (hip, IR) out for the year and Goodson now on IR, Israel Abanikanda -- who was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday -- will serve as Dallas' RB2 behind Javonte Williams for Sunday's game against the 49ers. Goodson is required to miss at least four games while on IR, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Rams on Sunday, Dec. 20.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - ACL + MCL

injuryReports.name: KaVontae Turpin
injuryReports.returnComment: Turpin has missed the Cowboys' last three games while recovering from a rib injury that he suffered in Week 6 against the Packers. His return will bolster Dallas' special teams, as he is the top returner on kickoffs and punts, and he'll also give the offense a boost as an explosive playmaker.
injuryReports.injury: Turpin (ribs) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: George Pickens
injuryReports.returnComment: After being listed as limited on five consecutive injury reports going back to last week due to a hamstring issue, Pickens practiced fully Friday and thus is set to miss just one game as a result. In eight appearances so far this season, he's talled a 39-533-2 line on 62 targets.
injuryReports.injury: Pickens (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: DeMarvion Overshown
injuryReports.returnComment: Overshown didn't play in the Week 9 win over the Colts. He was limited in Wednesday's practice, though after logging a full session Thursday, he is good to go for Sunday's meeting with the 49ers. The 26-year-old has appeared in only three games during the 2026 campaign, amassing 20 total tackles (eight solo) and one interception.
injuryReports.injury: Overshown (hamstring/back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Caleb Downs
injuryReports.returnComment: Squaring off with his older brother Josh Downs on the opposite side, Downs recorded his first career interception on the Colts' final offensive play of the game with 41 seconds left in the fourth quarter. On a pass intended for Keenan Allen, Downs picked off Daniel Jones to seal the four-point win. The first-round rookie Downs now has 55 tackles (32 solo), including 2.0 sacks, three pass breakups, with the interception, and a pair of forced fumbles on 93 percent of the defensive snaps across nine starts this season.
injuryReports.injury: Downs recorded three tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass breakups, including an interception, in Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Luke Schoonmaker
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end has missed the past two games for Dallas, but appears to be ready to return and could see significant snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford while Jake Ferguson (knee) is sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Schoonmaker (groin) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Devin Moore
injuryReports.returnComment: The fourth-round rookie cornerback has yet to play in a game this season after being placed on injured reserve ahead of the Week 1 opener. Once he does return to action, Moore will provide depth behind Joey Porter (ankle), DaRon Bland, Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant.
injuryReports.injury: Hip

injuryReports.name: Ryan Flournoy
injuryReports.returnComment: Flournoy had a chance to operate in a more prominent role on offense with George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, but Flournoy ultimately finished with his fewest catches since Week 3, despite playing 77 of 79 offensive snaps. The wide receiver helped set up Dallas for the game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, reeling in a deep ball from quarterback Dak Prescott for a 46-yard gain. Flournoy now has reeled in 32 of 47 targets for 395 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Flournoy caught two of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Brevyn Spann-Ford
injuryReports.returnComment: Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the season thus far, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine contests.
injuryReports.injury: Spann-Ford caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win versus the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Brandon Aubrey
injuryReports.returnComment: Aubrey was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game, but he did miss a kick for the second straight week. The kicker had makes from 45 and 28 yards in the contest, but he continued his long-range struggles Sunday, pulling a 50-yard attempt wide left late in the fourth quarter. Aubrey has now gone 17-for-22 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-8 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests to open the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Aubrey went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.

injuryReports.name: Dak Prescott
injuryReports.returnComment: Prescott had a couple of bumps in the road against an inconsistent Colts defense, but the veteran signal-caller, who was also working without George Pickens (hamstring), still found his way to his third 300-yard effort of the season. Prescott unsurprisingly bestowed plenty of attention on CeeDee Lamb, who ultimately was responsible for 10 of his completions, 195 of his yards and one of his two TDs. Prescott also connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard scoring strike early in the second quarter, and the one blemish on the star quarterback's day was a  fumble on a sack at his own 16-yard line that led to a Colts touchdown. Prescott has at least one touchdown pass in every game heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Prescott completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for one yard in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Javonte Williams
injuryReports.returnComment: Williams turned in one of his more efficient performances against an inconsistent Colts defense, ultimately managing his second 100-yard effort of the season. Williams continued to serve as a prolific supplier of touchdowns as well, recording his ninth rushing score of the campaign on a one-yard run with 1:08 remaining to seal the victory for Dallas. Williams' week-to-week yardage production has fluctuated a fair amount, but his high-volume role and trusted red-zone presence keeps him a must-play despite a tough Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers next Sunday.
injuryReports.injury: Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Malik Benson
injuryReports.returnComment: Benson is a healthy scratch for a third consecutive week. The rookie sixth-rounder has failed to find a place in a wide-open receiving corps so far, and it remains to be seen how coach Klint Kubiak will utilize him.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Thomas Booker IV
injuryReports.returnComment: Booker was a full participant in Friday's practice but remained questionable headed into the weekend. The defensive lineman appears to not be quite ready to suit up, leaving JJ Pegues to see more defensive snaps in Sunday's contest.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Dont'e Thornton Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: Thornton was a late addition to the Raiders' injury report due to a back issue. It's been determined by medical staff that the second-year wide receiver will not play in Sunday's contest, and Thornton has yet to play in a regular-season game in 2026 after appearing in 15 contests during his rookie campaign. Dareke Young and Cody White will operate as the depth options at wide receiver behind Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Tristin McCollum
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Dalton Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Bryce Cabeldue
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Carter Runyon
injuryReports.returnComment: Runyon began the season on IR due to a foot injury. He was activated Nov. 4 but was then waived the following day. Runyon subsequently returned to Las Vegas as part of the practice squad and could get his first regular-season game action of the campaign Sunday. However, the Raiders have three tight ends ahead of him on the depth chart (Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas), so Runyon may be limited to special teams if he does suit up.
injuryReports.injury: The Raiders elevated Runyon from their practice squad to the active roster Saturday.

injuryReports.name: Trey Zuhn III
injuryReports.returnComment: Zuhn started Week 10 prep with a pair of limited practices before upgrading to full participation in Friday's session. The starting left guard has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the defending champion Seahawks.
injuryReports.injury: Zuhn (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Folorunso Fatukasi
injuryReports.returnComment: Fatukasi popped up on the Raiders' injury report Wednesday with shoulder and back issues, but it seems like those were minor, and he's in line to suit up in Week 10. He figures to start on the defensive line Sunday versus the Seahawks.
injuryReports.injury: Fatukasi (shoulder/back) was a full participant at practice Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Treydan Stukes
injuryReports.returnComment: Stukes jumped in front of a Brock Purdy pass intended for George Kittle midway through the third quarter, although the Raiders' offense gave the ball right back to the 49ers two plays later on a Brock Bowers fumble. It was the second interception of the season for Stukes, who was a second-round selection of the Raiders in the 2026 NFL Draft. The rookie out of Arizona is up to 43 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through the first eight regular-season games of his NFL career.
injuryReports.injury: Stukes registered five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Jeremy Chinn
injuryReports.returnComment: Chinn finished Week 9 as the Raiders' third-leading tackler behind Nakobe Dean (19) and Quay Walker (11). Dean has logged at least seven stops in five consecutive outings, and he has accumulated 66 tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries over nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Chinn recorded nine tackles (six solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Quay Walker
injuryReports.returnComment: It was the second time in three games that Walker finished with double-digit stops, and he finished second on the Raiders in tackles behind Nakobe Dean (19). Walker is on track for his fifth consecutive 100-plus tackle campaign and is up to 72 stops (28 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.
injuryReports.injury: Walker posted 11 tackles (three solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Nakobe Dean
injuryReports.returnComment: Dean played every defensive snap and was all over the field in Week 9, finishing with a career-best 19 total tackles. He's logged at least 12 tackles in six of his last seven outings, and through nine regular-season games he has accumulated 98 total tackles, which is second-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (107).
injuryReports.injury: Dean logged 19 tackles (seven solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.

injuryReports.name: Aidan O'Connell
injuryReports.returnComment: O'Connell is set to back up rookie Mendoza, who replaced recently traded Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback. O'Connell has been with Las Vegas since the team drafted him in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The 28-year-old last appeared in a regular-season game in 2025, completing 10 of 22 attempts for 102 yards.
injuryReports.injury: O'Connell moves to QB No. 2 on the depth chart behind Fernando Mendoza, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.

injuryReports.name: Jack Bech
injuryReports.returnComment: Bech logged a 34 percent offensive snap share, third-highest among Raiders wideouts behind Jalen Nailor (74 percent) and Tre Tucker (64 percent). Though he seems fairly secure in the No. 3 wideout role, Bech hasn't done much this season, producing no more than three catches or 25 yards in any of his five games to date.
injuryReports.injury: Bech caught one of two targets for nine yards Sunday in a loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Fernando Mendoza
injuryReports.returnComment: The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has opened his professional career on the bench, with his lone action to date coming during garbage time of a blowout loss to the Patriots in Week 5, when he completed six of eight pass attempts for 48 yards. However, with the 4-5 Raiders shipping out Cousins for a 2027 third-round pick, the 23-year-old Mendoza will now be thrust into his first extended NFL playing time and will face a pair of tough defenses off the bat, as he'll follow up the matchup against the Seahawks with a road game in Denver in Week 11. Mendoza had underwhelming numbers over his three preseason appearances, but he's reportedly been "tearing it up in practice" during the regular season and has given the Raiders optimism that he's ready to lead the offense, per Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com.
injuryReports.injury: Mendoza will take over as the Raiders' new starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game versus the Seahawks after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Tuesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.

injuryReports.name: Matt Gay
injuryReports.returnComment: Gay's lone field goal came from 50 yards in the second quarter, and he now has made three of his four kicks from 50 yards or longer on the season. The 32-year-old is 19-for-21 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 21-for-21 on extra-point tries across nine appearances.
injuryReports.injury: Gay converted his only field-goal attempt and both of his extra-point tries during Las Vegas' loss to the 49ers on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jalen Nailor
injuryReports.returnComment: Nailor was a non-factor on offense in Week 9, failing to reach double-digit receiving yards for the fourth time this season. The wide receiver has had a hard time getting into a groove in his first season with Las Vegas, catching 14 of 28 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown over eight contests so far.
injuryReports.injury: Nailor caught two of four targets for nine yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Michael Mayer
injuryReports.returnComment: The tight end was inches and a couple breaks away from having a much bigger afternoon, as he lost a fumble just before crossing the goal line on what would have been a 25-yard touchdown. He then had another score called back on a penalty in the second half. Mayer has alternated big games with down ones this season, and he'll try to rebound next Sunday in a tough spot against the Seahawks' strong defense.
injuryReports.injury: Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Mike Washington Jr.
injuryReports.returnComment: The rookie running back wasn't targeted in the passing game. One week after getting a trial run as the Raiders' clear lead back, a game in which he produced 83 yards on 25 carries, Washington was out-snapped 32 to 17 by Ashton Jeanty against San Francisco. He's averaging just 3.9 yards per carry on 71 totes this season and has just three receptions, though it's worth noting that Jeanty has been even less efficient as a ball carrier with only 3.1 YPC. Washington is a fantasy bench stash, but the Raiders' rushing attack seems broken as a whole.
injuryReports.injury: Washington turned six carries into minus-three yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Tre Tucker
injuryReports.returnComment: Tucker finished tied for the team lead in targets with tight end Brock Bowers, garnering at least five targets for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The wide receiver rebounded well after being blanked in Week 8 versus the Jets, securing four or more receptions for the seventh time this season. Tucker has now reeled in 33 of 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns over the Raiders' first nine games during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Tucker caught four of eight targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Ashton Jeanty
injuryReports.returnComment: The Raiders largely abandoned the run after going down 14-0 early, but Jeanty was more effective with his six carries than Mike Washington, who rushed six times for minus-3 yards and finished without a target. Sunday's even distribution in carries was a positive development for Jeanty, who had just two rushing attempts to Washington's 25 in the Week 8 win over the Jets. Jeanty still has more receiving yards (371) than rushing yards (362) and is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry heading into a difficult Week 10 matchup against Seattle's elite front seven.
injuryReports.injury: Jeanty rushed six times for 25 yards while catching five of seven targets for minus-5 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Brock Bowers
injuryReports.returnComment: Bowers had a 21-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter and came one yard short of scoring again on a 33-yard catch on a fourth-quarter drive that ended with a Kirk Cousins interception in the end zone. The star TE has reached 70 receiving yards in all seven of his appearances this season and is up to six touchdowns. Bowers came five receiving yards shy of his season high and continues to roll, even as the 4-5 Raiders drop out of contention in the AFC. He'll likely face more resistance in Week 10 against the Seahawks, who just held Cardinals TE Trey McBride to 54 yards.
injuryReports.injury: Bowers caught seven of eight targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for two yards and lost a fumble.

injuryReports.name: Darien Porter
injuryReports.returnComment: Porter suffered a groin injury last Sunday against the Jets and logged a DNP/LP/FP practice progression this week. He was questionable to suit up entering Sunday but will ultimately be able to give it a go. Porter ranks second on the Raiders with five defensed passes on the season.
injuryReports.injury: Porter (groin) is active for Sunday's Week 9 battle against the 49ers.

injuryReports.name: Cody White
injuryReports.returnComment: White was released by the team Tuesday to make room for Carter Runyon (foot), who was activated off injured reserve. With Runyon now waived and potentially joining the Raiders' practice squad, White was re-signed. To date, the 27-year-old has had the best season of his career, amassing eight catches (19 targets) for 112 yards and three touchdowns.
injuryReports.injury: White was signed by the Raiders on Thursday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Ladd McConkey
injuryReports.returnComment: McConkey's next chance to play will thus arrive Nov. 22 against the Jets. In his absence versus Baltimore, Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith will be available to lead Los Angeles' WR corps.
injuryReports.injury: Back

injuryReports.name: Branson Taylor
injuryReports.returnComment: Taylor sat out every Chargers practice this week, so it's not surprising that he's not going to be able to play Monday. The second-year offensive tackle has worked in a rotational role when healthy this season, so his absence will affect the Chargers' depth along the offensive line.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Trey Pipkins III
injuryReports.returnComment: Pipkins hasn't played since Week 1 due to a knee injury. He was placed on IR in late September and had his 21-day practice window opened this past Thursday. The Chargers will need to activate Pipkins from injured reserve in order for him to be eligible to suit up Monday.
injuryReports.injury: Knee

injuryReports.name: Kayode Awosika
injuryReports.returnComment: Awosika hasn't played since Week 2, when he suffered a leg injury against the Raiders. The 28-year-old managed a full practice Saturday following limited sessions Thursday and Friday, so he has a genuine chance of returning to action Monday. Awosika will likely return to a starting role at left guard if he's able to suit up.
injuryReports.injury: Lower Leg

injuryReports.name: Kendall Williamson
injuryReports.returnComment: It will be the second straight absence for Williamson after he hurt his calf in Week 8 against the Rams. His absence will be felt on special teams, where he has logged all of his snaps so far this season.
injuryReports.injury: Calf

injuryReports.name: Isas Waxter
injuryReports.returnComment: Waxter was hurt in the first quarter last Sunday against Houston and couldn't return to the contest. He was unable to practice at all this week and has thus been ruled out for Monday Night Football. Waxter has played in four games so far this season, logging eight tackles (seven solo) over 44 defensive snaps and 26 snaps on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Deane Leonard
injuryReports.returnComment: Leonard suffered a concussion at some point between the Chargers' Week 6 loss to Kansas City and the team's Week 7 bye. He missed the club's past two contests but has now passed through the NFL's concussion protocol and has been cleared to return to game action. Leonard should assume a rotational role in Los Angeles' secondary.
injuryReports.injury: Leonard (concussion) does not have a designation for Monday's matchup against Baltimore.

injuryReports.name: Justin Eboigbe
injuryReports.returnComment: Eboigbe hurt his ankle last Sunday against Houston and missed Thursday's practice. He was able to log limited sessions Friday and Saturday, however, to give himself a chance to play Monday. If Eboigbe can't give it a go, Nick Barrett could pick up many of his defensive snaps.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Denzel Perryman
injuryReports.returnComment: Perryman has missed the entire season to date due to a pectoral injury. He was designated to return Nov. 4 and logged an LP/FP/FP practice progression this week. Perryman would have to be activated from IR in order to make his season debut Monday.
injuryReports.injury: Pectoral

injuryReports.name: Keaton Mitchell
injuryReports.returnComment: Mitchell's practice reps were limited by a hip injury, but he's been officially cleared to play Monday against the team he spent three seasons with from 2023 to 2025. He turned 10 touches into 67 yards during the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, and Mitchell will continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield alongside Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal.
injuryReports.injury: Mitchell (hip) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: David Njoku
injuryReports.returnComment: Njoku continues to progress in his recovery from fibula injury that landed him on injured reserve in late September. The veteran tight end turned eight targets into six catches for 67 yards across the first two games of the regular season prior to his injury, and his return would result in a reduced offensive workload for Oronde Gadsden.
injuryReports.injury: Lower Leg

injuryReports.name: Brenen Thompson
injuryReports.returnComment: doubtful
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Cam Hart
injuryReports.returnComment: Hart upgraded to full participation in Friday's practice after being limited during Thursday's session. The cornerback therefore should be set to suit up for Monday night's contest against the Ravens.
injuryReports.injury: Hart (ankle) practiced in full Friday.

injuryReports.name: Tre' Harris
injuryReports.returnComment: After being limited the day before, Harris erased any doubt about his availability for Monday's game at Baltimore. He saw a team-high seven targets on a 79 percent route share last week, catching three passes for a mere six yards in the 44-22 loss to Houston. Harris' volume projection for Week 10 partially depends on Ladd McConkey (back), who didn't play any snaps last week and didn't practice Thursday or Friday.
injuryReports.injury: Harris (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice.

injuryReports.name: Justin Herbert
injuryReports.returnComment: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh previously noted that the QB "should be good to go" for Week 10 action after imaging on Herbert's injured left middle finger came back negative for a fracture, per ESPN.com. The fact that Herbert isn't listed in any way on the team's first injury report this week aligns with that and paves the way for him to continue to helm the offense for 0-8 Los Angeles versus Baltimore.
injuryReports.injury: Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.

injuryReports.name: Daiyan Henley
injuryReports.returnComment: A trade involving Henley was agreed to Tuesday pending a physical, but the Broncos apparently found a red flag concerning his knee during that physical. Denver offered an updated trade to the Chargers with different draft compensation than the originally agreed upon 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, but the two sides were unable to agree on an updated framework, so Henley will ultimately remain with the Chargers. Henley has not missed a game this season, so the concern Denver discovered on his physical isn't expected to impact his availability for Monday's game against the Ravens.
injuryReports.injury: Henley remains with the Chargers, as the Broncos have backed out of trading for the linebacker, Jeff Legwold of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: KeAndre Lambert-Smith
injuryReports.returnComment: Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey couldn't play due to back spasms. If McConkey is also sidelined next Monday in Baltimore, Lambert-Smith could again be a fairly big part of Los Angeles' air attack.
injuryReports.injury: Lambert-Smith registered one catch (on four targets) for 50 yards in Sunday's loss to Houston.

injuryReports.name: Kimani Vidal
injuryReports.returnComment: The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.
injuryReports.injury: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets.

injuryReports.name: Oronde Gadsden
injuryReports.returnComment: Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.
injuryReports.injury: Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Charlie Kolar
injuryReports.returnComment: Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.
injuryReports.injury: Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Cameron Dicker
injuryReports.returnComment: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.
injuryReports.injury: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.

injuryReports.name: DJ Uiagalelei
injuryReports.returnComment: Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.
injuryReports.injury: Uiagalelei completed two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown after replacing Justin Herbert (finger) in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the game that Herbert could have a fractured finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Joe Cardona
injuryReports.returnComment: Cardona will end up missing a third consecutive game while recovering from an ankle injury, and his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Jake McQuaide will once again serve as the Rams' long snapper.
injuryReports.injury: Ankle

injuryReports.name: Trent McDuffie
injuryReports.returnComment: McDuffie missed three of the Rams' last four games due to a persistent back injury. The cornerback is all set to suit up for Sunday's game, as he and Cam Curl return to reinforce the Rams' secondary in time for a divisional matchup with the Cardinals' rookie quarterback Carson Beck.
injuryReports.injury: McDuffie (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Kam Curl
injuryReports.returnComment: Curl's sole limited practice session Friday was enough to cement his availability for Sunday's contest. The strong safety has started every contest for the Rams in 2026, playing 100 percent of the defensive snaps in six of the Rams' nine games.
injuryReports.injury: Curl (toe) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Davis Allen
injuryReports.returnComment: Allen has recovered enough from the oblique injury he suffered during the Rams' Week 9 win over the Commanders to suit up for Week 10. The No. 3 tight end is a key part of the Rams' 13-personnel offense, and he should continue seeing a significant share of offensive snaps for the team.
injuryReports.injury: Allen (oblique) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

injuryReports.name: Ty Simpson
injuryReports.returnComment: Simpson continues to be inactive behind Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett. The quarterback will only enter the game if both Stafford and Bennett must exit due to injury, illness or ejection.
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Keagen Trost
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Darryl Peterson III
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Maximus Pulley
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Desjuan Johnson
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Coach's Decision

injuryReports.name: Steve Avila
injuryReports.returnComment: inactive
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Myles Garrett
injuryReports.returnComment: Garrett was listed as limited on the Rams' first two Week 10 practice reports due to a knee injury and then got a veteran's rest day Friday, heading into the weekend listed as questionable. Head coach Sean McVay told Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com on Friday that Garrett is expected to play Sunday, which now has been confirmed. Garrett will be looking to have a similar impact to the 3.0-sack day he had in Week 9 against the Commanders.
injuryReports.injury: Garrett (knee) is listed as active Sunday at Arizona, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.

injuryReports.name: Davante Adams
injuryReports.returnComment: Rapoport also noted Sunday that Adams' fellow WR Puka Nacua (knee/toe) has an estimated return in the mid-December range. For now, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are in line to lead the WR corps of the Rams (who are on bye in Week 11), with CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also on hand.
injuryReports.injury: Hamstring

injuryReports.name: Puka Nacua
injuryReports.returnComment: After the Rams placed Nacua on injured reserve Thursday, Nacua must miss at least four games, which means his earliest return date is Sunday, Dec. 20 against the Cowboys. Considering the timeline given in Rapoport's report, Nacua thus may miss only the minimum number of contests while on IR after suffering PCL and MCL sprains and also a turf-toe injury last Sunday at Washington. With Davante Adams (hamstring) out at least one more outing, L.A. is rolling with a receiving corps of Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley in Week 10.
injuryReports.injury: Knee - MCL

injuryReports.name: CJ Daniels
injuryReports.returnComment: Daniels has seen minimal playing time this season, but he'll be thrust into a more prominent role offensively due to both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being on injured reserve. As such, Daniels -- a sixth-round selection of the Rams in the 2026 NFL Draft -- is slated to serve as the team's WR3 behind Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, with Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also in the mix for snaps on offense. During his final college season in Miami, Daniels recorded 50 catches for 557 yards and seven touchdowns across 13 games.
injuryReports.injury: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Daniels "will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward," Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.

injuryReports.name: Colby Parkinson
injuryReports.returnComment: Parkinson hasn't shown much hint of matching last year's TD-fueled fantasy production, but he could see more targets in the coming weeks with both Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve. Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are the favorites for WR snaps, likely leaving the RBs and TEs to handle a larger-than-usual portion of Matthew Stafford's targets. Of course, the Rams will probably want to run the ball more often while their top receiving weapons are sidelined.
injuryReports.injury: Parkinson (ribs) and Tyler Higbee (illness) have been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Tyler Higbee
injuryReports.returnComment: With wideout Puka Nacua (knee) placed on injured reserve this week, there's renewed fantasy interest in the Rams' tight ends. Higbee has run a lot of routes without providing production in recent games, but both he and Parkinson could see more targets over the next few weeks, including Sunday in a favorable matchup with Arizona's subpar pass defense.
injuryReports.injury: Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (rib) have both been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

injuryReports.name: Konata Mumpfield
injuryReports.returnComment: Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell have taken most of the WR snaps alongside Nacua since Adams landed on injured reserve. It now sounds like Adams may return in a few weeks, while Nacua is out for at least a month and uncertain beyond that. There's a big opportunity ahead, but Mumpfield has been targeted on just 23 of 168 routes (13.7 percent), which is a low rate even for someone sharing the field with Nacua/Adams. Atwell has an even lower target rate (11.6 percent), so the Rams likely need their RBs and TEs to take on more offensive burden in Nacua's absence. While targets aren't assured, Mumpfield does seem like the safest bet to log a lot of WR snaps over the next few weeks.
injuryReports.injury: Mumpfield will take on an increased role for the Rams while Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) are unavailable, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports.

injuryReports.name: Brennan Presley
injuryReports.returnComment: Los Angeles is hurting at wide receiver, so the team signed Presley to bolster depth. The 24-year-old has appeared in just one game during his NFL career since going undrafted in 2025, though he spent all of his time on special teams.
injuryReports.injury: The Rams signed Presley to the 53-man roster Thursday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.

injuryReports.name: Nate Landman
injuryReports.returnComment: Much like last season, when Landman set a career high with 132 tackles across 17 starts, he's racking up the tackles through eight games in 2026. The middle linebacker is up to 66 tackles (37 solo), three forced fumbles and two pass breakups on 86 percent of the defensive snaps. Interestingly, Landman's snaps have been cut some since he returned from a concussion in Week 8. Over the last two weeks, he's played less than 70 percent of the defensive snaps after playing more than 90 percent across Weeks 1 through 6.
injuryReports.injury: Landman recorded seven tackles (three solo), one pass breakup and a forced fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Quentin Lake
injuryReports.returnComment: Lake was credited with a forced fumble on the final play of the game, where Washington was trying to lateral the football down the field. Byron Young made the recovery for the Rams to clinch the win. For the season, Lake has recorded 63 tackles (37 solo) and has already set career highs in pass breakups (11), interceptions (three) and forced fumbles (two). He's also on pace to set a new career high in tackles.
injuryReports.injury: Lake recorded seven tackles (three solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.

injuryReports.name: Tutu Atwell
injuryReports.returnComment: Atwell ended up finishing second among Rams wide receivers in both targets and offensive snaps behind Puka Nacua. However, the Rams' offense will have to undergo a sizable overhaul in the absence of Nacua, who suffered a sprained PCL/MCL in his knee as well as turf toe during Sunday's win, with the superstar wide receiver expected to be sidelined for at least a month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. Davante Adams (hamstring) is also on injured reserve, so that leaves Atwell and Konata Mumpfield as the top healthy wide receivers on the Rams' 53-man roster, and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels is also in position for a larger role on offense. The Rams will face the Cardinals in Week 10, and Arizona's defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns on the year, which is second-most in the league behind Las Vegas' 20.
injuryReports.injury: Atwell recorded two catches on five targets for 16 yards during the Rams' 20-13 win over the Commanders on Sunday.

injuryReports.name: Jordan Whittington
